headline: Calibrating single-cell and spatial inference after imputation and spatial dependence
label: Computational Single Cell Modeling
summary: Imputed spatial transcriptomes, multi-omics similarity, and single-cell normalization now demand explicit error modeling for valid inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is statistical validity of inference in single-cell, spatial, and multi-omics data, where imputation, normalization, or spatial dependence must be modeled explicitly. TIDEST calibrates differential expression on imputed spatial transcriptomes, and sbivar and CONCISE account for spatial autocorrelation in bivariate association and ligand-receptor inference. A compound negative binomial extension of Pearson residuals handles scRNA-seq without UMIs, and power-law distance penalties correct long-range overestimation in single-cell co-accessibility. SEMFA and a stability-driven sparse GCCA framework address significance and reproducibility in multi-omics integration, while batch-effect work shows classifier bias in aggregated data. Atlases and portals, including the Human Pancreas Cell Atlas and ScPCA Portal, provide reference and data infrastructure rather than inferential methods. What is new is calibration after imputation, normalization, or spatial dependence rather than descriptive calling alone.
